verdict.rationale: Solid leans on familiar foundations. Components are regular JavaScript functions that run once, and the docs say you "don't have to learn a new rendering system." A `<div>` is a real DOM div, it gives direct DOM access for native libraries, and it is built on established JSX and TypeScript. Community reports from React and Vue users ("refs are just the elements", "looks like React, easier to understand") back up the low friction. However, components are written in JSX rather than plain HTML, and hands-on users name Solid-specific concepts that add learning: the special props object, props needing to be functions to stay reactive, and a reactivity API one user found non-intuitive. Missing for 10: plain HTML templating rather than JSX, any evidence on CSS authoring, freedom from Solid-specific reactivity concepts and prop rules, and docs aimed at newcomers.
